title: Native egress creation with fixed child network controls v3
description: Exact canonical sorted compact ensure_ascii JSON, including escaped DEL, with no LF, at most 32768 bytes and depth 6. Ed25519 signs the v3 payload schema ASCII, NUL, and exact canonical payload. Versions 1 and 2 are not upgraded by adding fields. The separate durable precreation claim authorizes fixed child-only manual network controls; no schema or signed grant alone is a durable claim, current proof, workload start or network attachment.

journal.description: Exact signed preprovisioned directory identity. creationJournal must differ from the kernel journal in path, device/inode pair and namespace; runtime enforces all three comparisons and actual protected directory ownership. Its separate SWNEGCR1 inventory admits at most 64 irreversible creation claims. Existing, partial, uncertain or historical claims never authorize another child. Local durability is not an off-host rollback witness.

childNetworkPolicy.description: Fixed fresh-child-only IPv4/IPv6 forwarding, router advertisement, autoconfiguration, redirect, solicitation and temporary-address controls. No caller-selected sysctl path or value. These creation-authorized controls precede attachment and do not authorize host mutation or application start.

payload.description: Exact 31-field pre-contact grant. All v1 semantic bounds and genuine setup/delegation/token/host joins remain mandatory, including the positive current i64-nanosecond interval of at most 300 seconds. Creation uses a stable purpose-separated slot from creationJournal.namespace and capability.capabilityId; the full grant and actual admitted proof/packet/configuration/CA bind its operation scope. Fresh evidence, process IDs or child identities cannot allocate a retry. A new child is possible only after an actual durable fresh claim; the separate kernel claim still precedes firewall mutation. The explicit attachment client requires this v3 grant and a separate signed network-attachment grant. No v3 egress grant alone authorizes exec/start, host attachment, recovery or repair.
